_comment: SHARED material INSPECTOR modal (scenes/shared/ - ruling 2A3592D0 R1: pop-up modals are shared modal TREES). Aaron 2026-10-21 (A5972856): pressing a box of the Material Catalog pops a centre-screen stage showing just that material and its graph read-only, with the material IN THE PACKAGE above and its DEFINITION below. SCENE-HOSTED, the settings precedent: its host is a scene of its own, `flicker_materialcatalog::MaterialInspector` (named in the shell's HOSTED_ELSEWHERE, exempted from the param seam's registry), because what it shows is LIVE - a turning lit sample on its own stage and the graph on a canvas - and the scene beneath a modal is frozen, so the modal scene owns them. It loads through `flicker_shell::hosted_modal_tree`, the parse path every shared modal uses, which writes the host's exit (`modal_cancel`) onto the root whatever this file says; Esc / pad-B and the Close button both fire it and the host answers `cancelled`. NEVER a trap: the slab is `dismissable` and nothing here holds it shut. The confirm.scene.json shape: a full-bleed `surface`, a scrim cell (layer 0), a centred `popup_panel` (layer 1). Its chrome (`modal.*`) rides Main's carrier; the blocks below are this tree's OWN (scene-owned styles, $tokens only), laid over the carrier by `flicker_shell::hosted_modal_styles`. Every string is a $token or a bound Model value the host publishes RAW (no pair script: every gate is a value the host already knows). EVERY SIZE IS AN ART PLACEHOLDER - Aaron's to tune in-window.

params._comment: The host's own configuration. `map_px`: the edge, in texels, a bundle's maps are decoded to (on a worker) before the sample wears them - the stage is about 390 px wide and a sphere shows half its texture's width at once, so 512 is ample. `canvas_fit_floor`: the zoom the graph is framed at on open when the whole graph would only fit smaller (the MaterialBench's `canvas_fit_floor`, so a card reads the same size in both). AARON'S TO TUNE - placeholders, never Rust constants.

inspector_sample._comment: The inspector's LIT SAMPLE - the `insp_sample` surface names this stage, and the engine's material-sample filler (flicker-materialview) draws the one material on a TURNING sphere (or plane) under it, LIVE. The `material` layer IS that body. The target clears TRANSPARENT ($stage_void) so the surface's authored well is the backdrop. Lighting, framing and the BLOOM are the MaterialBench's lit stage (`materialbench_lit`) - the same camera, because this box is the bench's size, not a catalog chip - so a material and its glow read here exactly as where it was made. EVERY NUMBER HERE IS AN ART PLACEHOLDER, Aaron's to tune in-window, never in Rust.
inspector_sample._emissive_gain: EMISSIVE GAIN - the draw-time multiplier on the material's Emit in this stage's HDR space (the host hands it to the sample's maps). ALL THREE lit stages must agree - this one, the Material Catalog's `mc_sample` and the MaterialBench's `materialbench_lit` (a gate holds them equal) - so a glow burns the same in the grid, in the inspector and where it was made. A finite number >= 0. AARON'S TO TUNE in-window - a placeholder, never a Rust constant.
inspector_sample._hdr: HDR: the `scene` pass renders the lit sample into the LINEAR rgba16f `hdr` working attachment, `bloom` spreads whatever crosses its threshold (an Emit at the gain above; a hot specular off low-roughness metal) into a halo, and `tonemap_grade` resolves it into the sRGB `color` LAST - the reads/writes ARE the order. Alpha passes through, so the transparent clear survives.

passes._comment: BLOOM - the SAME numbers as `mc_sample` and `materialbench_lit` (a gate holds the three equal), so a glow's halo reads alike everywhere. Art placeholders, tuned in-window.

material_inspector._comment: The full-screen SCRIM under the slab (the shared modals' dimmed backdrop). Authored as this tree's own block: it shadows the carrier's `screens` within this tree's resolution only, and nothing else here reads a `screens.*` block.

section._comment: The HEADER (in the package) and FOOTER (definition) panels.

well._comment: The backdrop well behind the lit sample and the graph canvas - each surface's own panel, drawn beneath what fills it (the sample clears transparent).

slider._comment: The zoom slider - the MaterialBench's `materialbench.slider` ink, so the control reads alike where the material is made and where it is shown, plus the focused ink a pad user lands on in the `modal` ring (every scene's own slider block authors the same keys). Theme tokens only.

canvas._comment: The graph canvas's colour slots (flicker_canvas::CanvasStyle) - the MaterialBench's canvas ink, so the graph reads alike where it is made and where it is shown. The filler owns no colour; every slot is a theme token here, resolved once when the inspector opens.
canvas.label: $ink_bright

children._comment: THE SLAB - `dismissable` (never held shut: this inspector runs no work a back-out could strand), titled with the material's name (`insp_title`, the host's resolved text). Its items stack: the PACKAGE header, the centre stage (lit sample + graph), the DEFINITION footer, the Close row. Its natural height (~860 px) fits 1600x900 and up; on a shorter screen (the shell's 1280x720 floor) the slab is CAPPED to the screen less `fit_margin` above and below and the CENTRE STAGE gives way (its `shrink`, down to its `min_size`) - the sample well and the canvas shrink, the header, the footer and the Close row keep their rows, and Close stays on screen. Sizes are Aaron's to tune.

HEADER - the material IN THE PACKAGE: what the promotion path holds for this slot (package, else staging, else nothing) and that bundle's facts, each a label token over a value the host publishes raw. `insp_pkg_note` says in words what the state means (nothing made yet / staged / promoted / a recipe that does not load).

CENTRE STAGE - LEFT the material on a turning lit body (`insp_sample` on `stages.inspector_sample`, LIVE) with the Sphere/Plane toggle under it (the MaterialBench's `lit_body`, labelled from the same tokens); RIGHT the graph, READ-ONLY - the host seats flicker_canvas::GraphCanvas in `insp_canvas` through flicker_materialview::graph_view (cards in evaluation order + the Output card with its port labels, framed legibly on open; wheel zooms, middle-drag pans, a click picks a card - nothing moves, nothing links), with the NODE LIST beside it (the pad's way to read a node). A picked card's `key · Kind`, its inputs and its parameters read out below. With no graph, `insp_graph_note` says why over the empty well.

The sample's ZOOM (the MaterialBench's `lit_zoom`, under this tree's name) - how close the material is drawn: the stage's camera distance divided by it (1 = the stage's own framing). The wheel over the sample moves the same number, one `step` per notch, inside this same range: the host reads `min` / `max` / `step` from THIS node, the one source - no param repeats them. It takes its height from the sample above it (the column is fixed; the slab is not). Pad: in the `modal` ring right after the body toggle, before the node rows; Left / Right step it. AARON'S TO TUNE - placeholders: min 1.0, max 4.0, step 0.25. `min` must stay in (0, 1] and `max` at least 1 (the sample opens on the stage's framing) and `step` above 0; anything else switches the zoom off, loudly.
children.label: $insp_zoom

children._comment: THE NODE LIST - the graph's cards as rows (the MaterialBench's `mtl_node_list` shape), in the canvas's own order: every node in evaluation order, then the Output. The pad's way to READ a node: the d-pad walks the rows (tab_group `modal`, after the body toggle and the zoom slider, and before Close) and Confirm picks one exactly as a click on its card does - the card wears the selection and the read-out below shows it. The host expands the ONE prototype per card (`rows_from: insp_nodes`, the walker's repeater) and publishes each row's label raw (`key · Kind`, the Output's heading); the list scrolls on its `insp_node_scroll` bind. Sizes are Aaron's to tune - but the list's width comes out of the CANVAS's: below about 576 px the canvas lays its cards out in ONE column, and a glow's five cards no longer frame whole at the legible floor (at 190 the canvas keeps ~590 px, two columns).

The picked card's READ-OUT, one line: its heading (`key · Kind`), then what feeds it (each port with the key wired there) beside its `$insp_lbl_inputs` label; its parameters wrap below. One line, not two, so the canvas keeps the height a glow needs to frame whole at the legible floor.

FOOTER - the material's DEFINITION: its row of the material index (materials.json) and the band its id is filed under (`_meta.bands`). Values are the row's own data; the render class is a token per class; the colour is a sprite over the 1x1 texture the host uploads in the index colour (`insp_swatch_tex`, absent for a free slot so it draws nothing). A FREE slot shows `$insp_unassigned` for its name and a dash for the rest. The three LONG-TEXT cells (band, represents, signature) WRAP onto a second line within their 30 px rather than running off their cell.

The way out, said plainly: Close fires the SAME exit Esc / pad-B fire (`modal_cancel`, the name the host was handed), so there is one way to leave and it always works. Its `nav_ordinal` 1001 keeps it LAST in the `modal` ring, after every node row the list can expand to (rows count up from 2, after the body toggle's 0 and the zoom slider's 1) - the MaterialBench's convention for buttons after its node list.
